memory_candidates.content: git-commit-scoped.sh's `git commit -- <pathspec>` RE-READS the working tree at commit time, regardless of any prior `git add`/`git apply --cached` partial staging. If a shared file carries both your own change and an unrelated concurrent task's uncommitted hunk, pre-staging only your hunk via `git apply --cached` does NOT protect it -- the commit will pick up the full current working-tree content for that path. To isolate your own change for a clean, scoped commit: temporarily revert the foreign hunk's own lines in the working file back to their HEAD value, run the commit, then immediately restore the foreign hunk's working-tree value afterward (never commit it, never discard it). Do this within the SAME phase before its one closing commit -- restoring and then committing again later risks a second, unrelated commit accidentally sweeping the foreign hunk back in if it is still listed in that phase's progress-file files_touched.

The validate-bounded-waiter.sh PreToolUse Bash hook refuses a command that combines a `kill -0` liveness check with a `pgrep -f`/`ps | grep` name-match probe in the SAME Bash invocation, even for a one-shot, non-loop diagnostic purpose (e.g. proving a name-based check would have matched a deliberately-injected test fixture). Split such checks into separate Bash calls. The hook is Bash-specific: authoring the same literal anti-pattern text as prose via the Write/Edit tools (e.g. documenting the forbidden shape in a standards file) is NOT blocked -- only an actual Bash tool invocation containing the pattern is.
